units.unit: The student is building an argument against a hard cap on SDU initial rents, in favor of tenure security plus a light indexed rent band.
The source carries the thesis sentence: a hard cap transfers modest gains to incumbents while shrinking stock available to new arrivals, single-parent families, and public-housing waiters.
All five sources are cited in the essay and cover the thesis, elasticity, stock data, and comparative cases.
The student needs sources behind the enforcement and landlord-behaviour sections.
The landlord-behaviour section makes a narrow claim: the Association's exit threat is weak evidence because it is self-reported and concedes no margin data.
The student needs the source to show the counter-view and its limits.
The student needs the tenant interview material for the Mrs Wong and Mr Chan points.
The essay's enforcement and remedy paragraphs rest on the enforcement capacity note, alternative-instrument note, and 2026 consultation document.
The student needs tenant interviews, landlord submission, and enforcement minute for cited claims.
The student still needs D12, the consultation document the essay's alternative package comes from.
D12 is the consultation document that floats the 'floor-standard + rent band' package.
D12 is the source for the final constructive claim that the indexed-band alternative is on the table for 2026.
The source is for the final constructive claim about the 2026 consultation.
